schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: The system device's answer to 'which box, which OS', published as a tool nested in the device: host_name() (the short hostname, lowercased, the roster's spelling) and os_id() (windows, linux, darwin). Every caller outside system_rackmount asks these two through this module and nothing else of the device's.
why: Akien, 2026-11-21: "hostname should come from the system device." Measured 2026-11-20: saveslate crashed on akiendell (Windows) at cairn/tools/base/claude_identity.py:108 because os.uname does not exist there. Saveslate auto-commit 4794006a7 moved the call into rackmount.py, which was the right home, but the path was unpublished: encapsulation_breaches read claude_identity.py into system_rackmount (RULE 1). A box has to be able to name itself with no bus running (saveslate, a recovery install), so the device publishes a tool rather than a bus verb.
entry: BUILT by ticket 5ccc7f05c932, 2026-11-21: host_name and os_id moved out of cairn/devices/system_rackmount/rackmount.py.
state_and_history: A TOOL HOLDS NO STATE OF ITS OWN (Law 6): it reads platform and writes nothing. Its first voyage, ticket 5ccc7f05c932, is owned by cairn/tools/base/ (the ticket names that charter as its owning intention), so the voyage records stand at that address, not beside this charter.
proof: proofs/test_the_host_tool_names_the_box.py (ticket 5ccc7f05c932, clause 3): with os.uname deleted, host_name() is short and lowercased; os_id() names an OS family; host.py imports no socket; and this charter publishes exactly its one module. Its first reader is proved in tools/base: cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_who_names_the_host_through_the_system_device.py.
gates: Import gate — encapsulation_holds in build_inspector (RULE 1, ticket 124c0312c2d8) admits a reach into system_rackmount only through this tool, because this charter says published_by_device. Seal: the tester seals the proof into validations/ beside it.
falsifier: Red if host_name() needs os.uname, or answers anything but the short lowercased name; if os_id() answers anything but windows/linux/darwin on those hosts; if host.py imports socket; or if this charter stops declaring published_by_device and exactly its one module.
how_it_learns: It does not; it reads platform, deliberately dumb physics.
traces_to: RULE 1 (encapsulation — a device's public interface is the bus plus any client tool it publishes)
Law 6 (a tool has users; system_rackmount holds the code)
Law 3 (the Windows behavior is measured at n=1 on akiendell)
owner: None of its own — a tool has users (Law 6): claude_identity first, then every caller spanning ticket B repoints. Its code is held by system_rackmount, which publishes it; CC gates writes to that code and its proofs.
